submission.justification: Absorber-F1 at 6 mm plate thickness provides the best energy resolution (3.951% at 100 GeV) among all configurations that meet the hard safety constraint. Absorber-F3, while offering better resolution, produces 85 uSv/h residual dose rate which exceeds the 20 uSv/h limit by more than 4x and therefore cannot be used. Absorber-F2 meets safety requirements but delivers inferior resolution (4.932% at best). The 6 mm thickness was determined by systematic optimization across the 2-10 mm range, showing a clear minimum in energy resolution at this value for Absorber-F1.

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 is listed in candidate_specs.md as a dense alloy candidate material

requirements.requirement: Residual dose rate at 1 m after one week of cooldown must not exceed 20 uSv/h for hands-on maintenance
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 produces 12 uSv/h residual dose rate according to activation_study_2026.md, which is below the 20 uSv/h limit. Absorber-F3 was excluded because it produces 85 uSv/h.
Recommended thickness of 6 mm is within the 2-10 mm constraint range

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Among viable options (F1 and F2), Absorber-F1 at 6mm achieves 3.951% resolution, which is the best achievable while meeting safety constraints. Systematic simulations from 2-10 mm confirmed 6 mm is optimal for F1.
